thread.title_full: Purdue campuses to cut or merge 83 programs ahead of new enrollment requirements - NewsBreak

author: EMERY DENHAM Staff Reporter
title: Purdue campuses to cut or merge 83 programs ahead of new enrollment requirements - NewsBreak
text: Eighty-three programs across Purdue campuses will be eliminated, suspended or consolidated ahead implementation of new requirements for enrollment, according to the Indiana Commission for Higher Education. The release of the program list on Monday came directly before the law went into effect on Tuesday. Section 248 of House Enrolled Act 1001 requires any degree program not meeting a specific enrollment threshold, averaged over the past three years, to be cut or consolidated. Alternatively, if an institution believes a low-enrollment program deserves to stay, it can submit an appeal to the ICHE. The thresholds for enrollment are 10 students for an associate degree program, 15 for a bachelor’s, seven for a master’s and three for a doctorate’s. A bulk of the programs affected are in Purdue’s two satellite campuses: Northwest and Fort Wayne. At the main West Lafayette campus, only seven programs will be subject to changes. Of these, two are slated for consolidation, four are suspended and a commitment has been made to suspend the last one. Suspended programs are planned for elimination but have been given a “teach out” period allowing students currently enrolled to finish their degree. “No currently enrolled program will be eliminated without an opportunity for currently enrolled students to complete their studies,” according to the commission. However, the same assurance is not given for the consolidation or merging of programs. A doctorate's and master’s in comparative literature are the two programs to be consolidated or merged into other majors at West Lafayette’s campus. Bachelor’s degrees in design and production, mathematics with computer science and microbiology will all be eliminated after their teach-out period, as will a master’s in health sciences. The program with a written commitment for suspension is a bachelor’s in art history. The rest of the 77 programs subject to changes are from the Purdue Northwest and Fort Wayne campuses, with 58 programs at Fort Wayne and 18 at Northwest. Most of the programs affected at both campuses are bachelor's degrees, and a vast majority of the Fort Wayne changes are merges or the commitment to merge. Only one program at Fort Wayne is going to be cut, with the other 57 set for consolidation in some way. All changes made at this point were listed by the commission as “voluntary early actions” before the implementation of the new law and don’t represent a comprehensive list of all underperforming degrees. “Voluntary early actions are not expected to apply to all under-threshold degree programs,” according to the commission in its guidance to higher education institutions. The commission provided colleges with data for 2021-23 fiscal years to base these early decisions on, but 2024 is still undergoing evaluation, which is needed to determine the three-year average that enrollment is based on. The commission expects to have the 2024 data by mid-July, after which they will work with each campus to create a Mutual Consensus List of under-performing programs. If an institution wishes to save a program on this list, then it must apply for approval.
